headings.title: Consent by minors over sixteen and under twenty-one

headings.title: Physician judgment on autopsy scope and liability protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section history note. Covers a licensed physician and surgeon exercising judgment on the scope and extent of an autopsy or postmortem examination performed with subsection 1 consent and the accompanying immunity from liability.

headings.title: Consent under section 194.170 for unclaimed dead
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section history note. Covers the prohibition on licensed physicians holding a postmortem examination on any unclaimed dead without the consent required by section 194.170, qualified by the exception when specifically authorized by law.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties under section 194.180 for unauthorized autopsies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and section history note. Covers both non-physicians performing an autopsy and licensed physicians acting without required authorization, making violators upon conviction guilty of a misdemeanor subject to section 194.180 penalties.

headings.title: Availability of autopsy reports upon request
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and section history note. Qualified to cases where an autopsy is performed on a deceased patient and a report is prepared, requiring availability upon request to the personal representative or estate administrator, surviving spouse, or any surviving child, parent, brother, or sister.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 9 subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(9) and paragraphs (5)(a)-(d) of sub 2), history note (L. 2003 H.B. 394 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 1696), and severability note (§ 1.1002), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Meaning of right of sepulcher
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 2003 H.B. 394 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 1696), and severability cross-reference (§ 1.1002). headings.title: Meaning and priority order of next-of-kin
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(9) and paragraphs (5)(a)-(d)), history note, and severability note (§ 1.1002). headings.title: Next-of-kin control and delegation under section 404.710
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history note, and severability note. Covers next-of-kin entitlement to control final disposition consistent with applicable laws and health codes, and permissive delegation to an agent under section 404.710 conditioned on age, competence, and principal or agent financial responsibility.

headings.title: Funeral director or establishment reliance and relative fault
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, history note, and severability note. Covers funeral director or establishment reliance on lawful instructions of a person claiming to be next-of-kin and possible reduction of relative fault in civil actions; retains archived source wording "licensed pursuant to this chapter" without altering it even though licensing appears in chapter 333.

headings.title: Notice required to persons with superior priority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, history note, and severability note. Covers the duty of any person desiring to exercise the right of sepulcher who knows of an individual or individuals with a superior right to notify them before making final arrangements.

headings.title: Waiver of superior right by nonobjection or writing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, history note, and severability note. Covers deemed waiver when a superior claimant notified in person or by delivery-confirmed written notice does not object within forty-eight hours, as well as voluntary dated written waiver at any time.

headings.title: Instructions and majority decisions within equal-priority classes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, history note, and severability note. Covers funeral director reliance on the first person in an equal-priority class when no objection is known (conditioned on cost assumption and absence of written objection), and majority control when the director knows equal-priority members disagree.

headings.title: Proxy voting for equal-priority class decisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8, history note, and severability note. Requires the funeral director to permit voting by proxy through a written authorization or instrument when conducting a majority vote under subsection 7.

headings.title: Consideration of the deceased's beliefs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9, history note, and severability note. Directs next of kin to consider the deceased person's religious, cultural, family, and individual beliefs when disposing of human remains.

headings.title: Establishment and membership of the anatomical board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (RSMo 1939 § 9998; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909), and Reorganization Act of 1974 cross-reference note (board transferred to department of higher education and workforce development, section 173.005). headings.title: Board control over disposal and delivery of bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and section 173.005 cross-reference note. Grants the board exclusive charge and control over disposal and delivery of dead human bodies described in sections 194.120 to 194.180 among entitled educational institutions.

headings.title: Secretary's records of received and distributed bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history note, and section 173.005 cross-reference note. entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (RSMo 1939 § 10003; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Institutional voting rights and annual meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 10003; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). headings.title: Bylaws, officers, agents, and compensation

headings.title: Institutional remittances and custody of board funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. headings.title: Sworn student-attendance statements for accepting institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9999; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Requires specified officials of institutions desiring to accept sections 194.120 to 194.180 to furnish a sworn attendance statement to the board secretary within thirty days of the first day of each term.

headings.title: Institutional bonds, prohibited trafficking or export, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Notice, delivery, and claim period for public-expense bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 10000; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). headings.title: Delivery expenses and local records of reported bodies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires receiving institutions to pay necessary delivery and notice expenses (including telegraph notice when needed) and requires reporting officers to furnish body records to the county clerk or St. Louis city health commissioner.

headings.title: Burial expense liability for failure to notify or deliver
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Imposes burial expense on a person who fails to notify and deliver a body as required when that failure renders the body unfit for anatomical purposes as certified by an authorized board officer or agent.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (RSMo 1939 § 10001; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked proportional distribution to compliant section 194.120 institutions under sections 194.120 to 194.180, permissive employment of carriers, enclosed transport free from public observation, and identifying custody receipts deposited with the board secretary. Both drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Proportional distribution of bodies to compliant institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 10001; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Directs the board secretary to distribute bodies to section 194.120 institutions that accept and comply with sections 194.120 to 194.180, in proportion to anatomy student attendance.

headings.title: Conveyance by carriers, enclosed transport, and custody receipts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits employing carriers, requires suitable encasement free from public observation, and requires carriers to obtain identifying receipts from custodians and deposit them with the board secretary.

headings.title: Hospital or facility notice, parental instructions, disposition, and costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Classifies any violation of section 194.200 as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(5)) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 43 § 2 through A.L. 2008 S.B. 1139). Covers DHSS establishing or contracting for the first person consent organ and tissue donor registry, non-obligation notice, legal consent upon registration (subject to subsection 2), withdrawal of registry consent, and DHSS/DOR advisories distinguishing withdrawal from a section 194.235 refusal and noting section 194.245 priority donation authority.

headings.title: Persons authorized to make lifetime anatomical gifts

Subject to section 194.240, enumerates who may make an anatomical gift during the donor's life under section 194.225 for transplantation, therapy, research, or education: eligible donors (adults, emancipated minors, or minors authorized to apply for a driver's license), non-prohibited agents, parents of unemancipated minors, and guardians.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections (including sub 1(1)-(4) and sub 2(1)-(2)) and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139, A.L. 2019 S.B. 368), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Methods for a donor to make an anatomical gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(4)) and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139, A.L. 2019 S.B. 368). Covers donor-made gifts via driver's license or ID card face statement/symbol or DHSS-issued back sticker, will, terminal illness or injury communication to at least two adults (at least one disinterested witness), or subsection 2 methods.

headings.title: Donor cards, signed records, registries, and assisted signing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)-(2)) and history note. Covers gifts by a donor or section 194.220 authorized person via signed donor card/record or donor registry statement/symbol, plus witnessing and attestation requirements when another signs for a physically unable signer. Retains archived source discrepancy in subdivision (2) citing "subdivision (1) of subsection 1 of this section" rather than subdivision (1) of subsection 2.

headings.title: License or identification card revocation, suspension, expiration, or cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides that revocation, suspension, expiration, or cancellation of a driver's license or identification card does not invalidate an anatomical gift indicated on it.

headings.title: Effect of gifts made by will
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Provides that an anatomical gift made by will takes effect upon the donor's death regardless of probate and is not invalidated by post-death invalidation of the will.

headings.title: Department website registration and mailed donor stickers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires DHSS to include organ donation information and a registration link on its website, check with DOR whether the donor symbol appears on the front of the registrant's license or ID card, and mail a back donor symbol sticker via first class mail if absent (referencing section 302.171).

headings.title: Optional state agency homepage links to donor registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Uses permissive language ("may") allowing all state agencies and departments to place a homepage link to DHSS organ donation information and registration.

headings.title: Amending or revoking by signed record or later document
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(2) and paragraphs (1)(a)-(c)) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 43 § 3, A.L. 2002 S.B. 1026, A.L. 2008 S.B. 1139). Subject to section 194.240, allows a donor or section 194.220 authorized person to amend or revoke a gift by signed record (including assisted signing subject to subsection 2) or by a later-executed document of gift expressly or by inconsistency.

headings.title: Witnessing requirements for records signed by another
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)-(2)) and history note. Sets two-adult witnessing (at least one disinterested witness) and attestation statement requirements for records signed under subsection 1(1)(c).

headings.title: Revoking by destroying or cancelling the document of gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Subject to section 194.240, allows a donor or section 194.220 authorized person to revoke a gift by destroying or cancelling the document of gift or relevant portion with intent to revoke.

headings.title: Terminal-illness or injury amendment or revocation of non-will gifts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits a donor to amend or revoke an anatomical gift not made in a will by any communication during terminal illness or injury addressed to at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness.

headings.title: Amending or revoking anatomical gifts made in a will
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits a donor who made an anatomical gift in a will to amend or revoke it in the manner provided for wills or under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including sub 1(1)-(3), sub 2(1)-(2), and sub 3(1)-(3)) and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Methods for refusing to make an anatomical gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(3) and paragraphs (1)(a)-(b)) and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139). Covers refusal by signed record (self or assisted signing subject to subsection 2), by will regardless of probate or post-death invalidation, or by communication during terminal illness or injury to at least two adults (at least one disinterested witness).

headings.title: Witnessing requirements for refusal records signed by another
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)-(2)) and history note. Sets two-adult witnessing (at least one disinterested witness) and attestation requirements for refusal records signed under subsection 1(1)(b).

headings.title: Methods for amending or revoking a refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1)-(3)) and history note. Permits amending or revoking a refusal via subsection 1 methods, a subsequent inconsistent anatomical gift under section 194.225, or destroying or cancelling the refusal record or portion with intent to revoke.

headings.title: Effect of unrevoked refusals on gifts by others
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Bars all other persons from making an anatomical gift when an unrevoked refusal exists, absent express contrary indication and except as provided in "subsection 8 of section 194.240"; retains archived source discrepancy explicitly because archived section 194.240 contains only subsections 1 through 7.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 43 § 4 through A.L. 2008 S.B. 1139), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Verified exact cross-references to sections 194.220, 194.225, 194.230, 194.245, and 194.250, donor vs. non-donor revocation distinctions in subs 2 and 4, part/purpose non-limitation rules in subs 5 and 6, and parent/guardian authority for deceased unemancipated minors in sub 7 (confirming no sub 8 exists). Revised sub 1 to cover making/amending/revoking and reflect sub 6, sub 7, and contrary-indication qualifications, and revised sub 3 to cover making as well as amending or revoking under section 194.250; retained subs 2 and 4-7.

headings.title: Limits on others overriding a donor's gift or amendment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 43 § 4 through A.L. 2008 S.B. 1139). Except as provided in subsection 7 and subject to subsection 6, absent express contrary donor indication, bars non-donors from making, amending, or revoking a gift of a donor's body or part made under section 194.225 or amended under section 194.230.

headings.title: Effect of donor revocation on later gifts by others
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Clarifies that a donor's revocation under section 194.230 is not a refusal and does not bar persons under section 194.220 or 194.245 from making a gift under section 194.225 or 194.250; distinguished from subsection 4 covering non-donor revocations.

headings.title: Bar on section 194.250 actions after another's pre-death gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars another person from making, amending, or revoking a gift under section 194.250 when a non-donor has made an unrevoked gift under section 194.225 or amendment under section 194.230.

headings.title: Effect of a non-donor's revocation on gifts by others
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Clarifies that a revocation under section 194.230 by a person other than the donor does not bar another person from making a gift under section 194.225 or 194.250; distinguished from subsection 2 covering donor revocations.

headings.title: Effect of one-part gifts on donating other parts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Absent express contrary indication by the donor or section 194.220 authorized person, provides that gifting one part is neither a refusal nor a limitation on later gifting another part.

headings.title: Effect of specifying purposes on gifts for other purposes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Absent express contrary indication by the donor or section 194.220 authorized person, provides that gifting a part for one or more section 194.220 purposes does not limit gifting it for other purposes under section 194.225 or 194.250.

headings.title: Parent or guardian revocation or amendment for unemancipated minors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Allows a reasonably available parent or guardian of a deceased unemancipated minor donor to revoke or amend an anatomical gift of the minor's body or part.

headings.title: Decisions and objections within multi-member priority classes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Bar when a prior-class member is reasonably available
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits making an anatomical gift if, at the time of the decedent's death, a person in a prior subsection 1 class is reasonably available to make or object to the gift.

headings.title: Execution of post-death anatomical gifts under section 194.245
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 43 § 5, A.L. 2008 S.B. 1139). headings.title: Amendment or revocation by reasonably available prior-class members

headings.title: Persons eligible to be named as gift recipients

Lists eligible named recipients: listed institutions, procurement organizations, or appropriate persons for research or education; a designated individual transplant recipient (subject to subsection 2); and eye or tissue banks.

headings.title: Disposition when a designated individual cannot receive a transplant
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Provides that if a part gifted to an individual under subsection 1(2) cannot be transplanted into that individual, it passes under subsection 7 absent express contrary indication.

headings.title: Passing of unnamed-recipient gifts that identify a purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1)-(4)) and history note. Sets passing rules for specific-part or all-part gifts naming no subsection 1 person but stating a purpose, routing eyes, tissue, and organs for transplantation/therapy to appropriate banks or OPOs and parts for research/education to appropriate procurement organizations.

headings.title: Priority when multiple purposes are listed without priority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. For subsection 3 gifts stating multiple unprioritized purposes, requires use for transplantation or therapy if suitable and permits research or education if unusable for transplantation or therapy.

headings.title: Specific-part gifts naming neither recipient nor purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Restricts specific-part gifts naming no subsection 1 recipient and stating no purpose to transplantation or therapy, passing under subsection 7.

headings.title: General-intent donor statements or symbols
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Restricts documents expressing only general donor intent (such as "donor", "organ donor", "body donor", or similar statements/symbols) to transplantation or therapy, passing under subsection 7.

headings.title: Default recipient rules and research or education fallback
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (subdivisions (1)-(4)) and history note. Applies to subsections 2, 5, and 6 by passing eyes to eye banks, tissue to tissue banks, organs to OPOs as custodian, and permitting medically unsuitable gifts to pass to procurement organizations for appropriate scientific or medical research or education.

headings.title: Organ procurement organization custody for nondesignated organ gifts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Provides that an anatomical gift of an organ for transplantation or therapy passes to the organ procurement organization as custodian, excluding designated-individual gifts under subsection 1(2).

headings.title: Custody of unused or nonpassing bodies and parts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Passes custody of a body or part to the person obligated to dispose of it if the gift does not pass under subsections 1 through 8 or is not used for transplantation, therapy, research, or education.

headings.title: Bar on accepting invalid or refused gifts and imputed knowledge
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Bars accepting a gift known to be ineffectively made under section 194.225 or 194.250 or barred by an unrevoked section 194.235 refusal, and deems knowledge of a document of gift to include any amendment, revocation, or refusal on the same document.

headings.title: Bar on knowingly accepting gifts from executed foreign prisoners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Prohibits accepting an anatomical gift if the person knows it is from the body of an executed prisoner from another country.

headings.title: No effect on organ allocation except designated recipients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Provides that except under subsection 1(2), nothing in "this act" affects organ allocation for transplantation or therapy; retains archived "this act" phrasing (no footnote appears on this section).

headings.title: Reasonable search for donor or refusal information

headings.title: Forwarding located donor or refusal documents to hospitals

headings.title: Liability immunity and possible administrative sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Shields persons from criminal or civil liability for failing to discharge section duties while preserving possible ("may be subject to") administrative sanctions.

headings.title: No lifetime delivery required for document effectiveness
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139). Establishes that a document of gift need not be delivered during the donor's lifetime to be effective.

headings.title: Post-death examination and copying of gift or refusal documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires any possessor of a document of gift or refusal upon or after an individual's death to allow examination and copying by persons authorized to make or object to a gift or persons to whom the gift could pass under section 194.255.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 11 subsections, history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2331 merged with S.B. 710), and footnote on 'this act*' (S.B. 1139 (2008) and H.B. 2331 merged with S.B. 710 (2022)), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Procurement organization search of registries and records upon referral
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2331 merged with S.B. 710), and footnote on "this act". Requires a procurement organization referred an individual at or near death by a hospital to reasonably search known geographic donor registries and applicable records.

headings.title: Procurement organization access to state agency donor records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Requires allowing a procurement organization reasonable access to DHSS and DOR records to determine whether an individual at or near death is a donor.

headings.title: Medical suitability examinations and limits on withdrawing measures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. headings.title: Post-death medical suitability examinations by gift recipients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes. Unless prohibited by law outside sections 194.210 to 194.294, permits a section 194.255 recipient at any time after death to conduct reasonable examinations of the body or part for medical suitability.

headings.title: Access to medical records during suitability examinations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section notes. Unless prohibited by law outside sections 194.210 to 194.294, permits examinations under subsection 3 or 4 to include all medical records of the donor, potential donor, or prospective donor.

headings.title: Parent search and revocation opportunity for unemancipated minors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and section notes. Requires a procurement organization, upon death of a minor donor or refuser not known to be emancipated, to conduct a reasonable search for the parents and give them an opportunity to revoke or amend the gift or revoke a refusal.

headings.title: Search for priority persons and notice of gift changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and section notes. Requires a procurement organization upon subsection 1 hospital referral to reasonably search for section 194.245 priority persons, and to promptly inform other recipients upon learning an anatomical gift to them was made, amended, or revoked.

headings.title: Recipient priority, acceptance or rejection, and remains handling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8, history note, and footnote (* "This act" in S.B. 1139 (2008) and H.B. 2331 merged with S.B. 710 (2022) contained numerous sections). Subject to sections 194.255(9) and 58.785, establishes superior recipient rights, whole or partial acceptance or rejection, permissible embalming/cremation/funeral use for whole-body gifts (subject to document terms and "this act*"), and part removal before embalming, burial, or cremation without unnecessary mutilation.

headings.title: Participation bar for attending and death-determining physicians
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and section notes. Prohibits both the physician attending the decedent immediately prior to or at death and the physician determining time of death from participating in removing or transplanting a part.

headings.title: Terminal-care bar for procuring physicians and procurement organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and section notes. Prohibits a removing or transplanting physician or procurement organization from having primary responsibility for health care treatment or decision-making for the individual's terminal condition during the donor hospitalization.

headings.title: Qualified physicians and technicians removing donated parts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and section notes. Authorizes a physician or technician to remove any donated part from a donor's body that the physician or technician is qualified to remove.

headings.title: Reasonable cost exclusions from valuable consideration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Excludes reasonable payments associated with removal, transportation, implantation, processing, preservation, quality control, and storage of any part or whole body from "valuable consideration" for this section.

headings.title: Immunity of gift makers and donors' estates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Protects both the person making an anatomical gift and the donor's estate from liability for any injury or damage resulting from making or using the gift.

headings.title: Reliance on relationship representations under section 194.245
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits relying on relationship representations by individuals listed in section 194.245(1)(2)-(8) when determining whether a gift was made, amended, or revoked under sections 194.210 to 194.294, unless known to be untrue.

headings.title: Resolving conflicts between directives and anatomical gift measures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Laws governing valid execution of a document of gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(3)) and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1139). headings.title: Missouri law governing interpretation of valid documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs that Missouri law governs interpretation of any document of gift valid under subsection 1.

headings.title: Presumption of validity absent contrary knowledge
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Allows a person to presume a document of gift or amendment is valid unless the person knows it was not validly executed or was revoked.

headings.title: Informed-consent requirement for out-of-state or foreign documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires out-of-state or foreign documents of gift to be executed by a record, document, or donor registry expressing informed consent to make an anatomical gift.

headings.title: Fund creation, deposit sources, and authorized uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 H.B. 178 § 1 subsec. 1, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2331 merged with S.B. 710). Establishes the Organ Donor Program Fund in the state treasury; directs depositing amounts received under sections 301.020, 301.3125, and 302.171(2) and other sources; specifies education, awareness, recognition, training, and registry uses (unless designated under subsection 4); and permits supporting section 194.300 advisory committee expenses.

headings.title: Department authority to pursue program funding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits ("may") DHSS to pursue funding supporting the programmatic efforts and initiatives outlined in subsection 1.

headings.title: Investment of excess fund balances and earnings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the state treasurer to invest fund balances exceeding $500,000 not needed for immediate disbursement or allocation under section 30.260 and credit all investment earnings to the fund.

headings.title: Acceptance and conditional use of public and private contributions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits the fund to accept gifts, grants, appropriations, and contributions from public or private sources (including sections 301.020, 301.3125, and 302.171), usable by DHSS per specified terms or conditions or otherwise for subsection 1 purposes.

headings.title: No state funding obligation from federal awards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Clarifies that accepting and using federal funds neither commits state funds nor obligates the general assembly to continue federally funded programs or activities.

headings.title: Fund administration, appropriation requirement, and committee consultation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs the state treasurer to administer the fund, limits DHSS use solely upon appropriation, and permits DHSS consultation with the organ donation advisory committee on programming and expenditures.

headings.title: Exemption from general revenue transfer and self-sustainability limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Exempts end-of-biennium balances from transfer to general revenue notwithstanding section 33.080 and prohibits general revenue appropriations to administer the fund if it cannot sustain itself.

headings.title: Compensation bar, expenses, terms, and service at pleasure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits compensation while permitting reimbursement of reasonable and necessary expenses from appropriations, sets five-year terms, and states members serve at the director's pleasure.

headings.title: Operational and twenty-four-hour access requirements for donor registries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)-(3)) and history note. headings.title: Limits on postoperative independent-living requirements with compensatory support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Checked immediate notice duty, 50-foot work stoppage and prompt resumption authorization for construction/agricultural earth-disturbing/archaeological discoveries, and legal-investigation vs. SHPO jurisdiction split (retaining archived wording 'local enforcement officer' in sub 2(2)). Both drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Immediate notice upon knowledge of disturbed or exposed burials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 3). Requires any person knowing or with reason to know an unmarked human burial or human skeletal remains are being disturbed, destroyed, defaced, mutilated, removed, excavated, or exposed to immediately notify either the state historic preservation officer or local law enforcement officer with jurisdiction.

headings.title: Work stoppage within fifty feet and jurisdiction determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)-(2)) and history note. Requires immediate cessation within a fifty-foot radius during construction, agricultural earth-disturbing activity, or archaeological investigation until authorized to resume by the responsible officer acting promptly within a reasonable time, and assigns jurisdiction to local law enforcement if a legal investigation may be involved or otherwise to the state historic preservation officer (noting archived text in subdivision (2) reads "local enforcement officer").

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 4), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked SHPO removal decision and general archaeological investigation for construction/agricultural discoveries (sub 1) versus archaeologist-discovery reporting (sub 2, retaining archived wording 'state historic officer'), 30-day reporting deadlines, and the 30-day maximum construction suspension/delay cap in sub 3. All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Preservation officer duties and investigations after earth-disturbing discoveries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 4). Covers construction or agricultural earth-disturbing discoveries under state historic preservation officer jurisdiction: officer decides whether removal for scientific analysis is necessary and appropriate, and a professional archaeologist conducts a general archaeological investigation and advises the officer of location and cultural/biological characteristics within thirty days of assumed jurisdiction.

headings.title: Archaeologist reporting after discoveries during archaeological investigations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by covering discoveries made by a professional archaeologist during an investigation under state historic preservation officer jurisdiction, requiring location and cultural/biological reporting within thirty days of assumed jurisdiction (retaining archived wording "state historic officer").

headings.title: Thirty-day limit on construction suspension or delay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars suspending or delaying construction for more than thirty days notwithstanding contrary provisions in the section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including sub 1(1)-(4)) and history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 5, A.L. 2018 S.B. 843), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked tiered kinship, ethnic-leader, and advisory-council consultations, skeletal-analyst review and 1-year or council-approved study delays (retaining archived wording 'subdivisions (2) and (3) of this section' and 'state historical preservation officer' in sub 1(4)), and federal NHPA/NAGPRA conformity in sub 2. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Kinship, ethnic, and council consultations and study delays
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(4)) and history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 5, A.L. 2018 S.B. 843). Sets disposition procedures upon reporting unmarked burials or remains to the state historic preservation officer: consulting closest kin, consulting ethnic-group leaders (with up to one-year reinterment delay for skeletal analysis if scientifically significant), consulting the Missouri advisory council on historic preservation for remains unrelated to living peoples (with council-adjustable delay), and seeking council approval for additional scientific study delays (retaining archived wording "subdivisions (2) and (3) of this section" and "state historical preservation officer" in subdivision (4)).

headings.title: Conformity with federal historic preservation and repatriation laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires all actions and decisions of the state historic preservation officer and advisory council to conform with the federal National Historic Preservation Act of 1966 (as amended) and the federal Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections, history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 7 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked entity/person coverage for knowingly disturbing marked or unmarked burial sites (class E felony) and escalating misdemeanor-to-felony commercial trafficking penalties for human remains and unlawfully obtained cultural items under sections 194.400-194.410 (noting section 194.400(5) definition of second or subsequent violation). Revised sub 3 from 'unlawful cultural items' to 'unlawfully obtained cultural items'; retained subs 1 and 2.

headings.title: Class E felony for knowingly disturbing human burial sites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1987 S.B. 24 § 7 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Makes knowingly disturbing, destroying, vandalizing, or damaging a marked or unmarked human burial site by any person or listed business/organization a class E felony.

headings.title: Penalties for unauthorized commercial dealings in human remains
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Covers knowingly appropriating or using for profit, selling, purchasing, or transporting for sale or profit human remains without right of possession under sections 194.400 to 194.410: class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for a second or subsequent violation (defined in adjacent unnumbered section 194.400(5) to include prior trafficking violations under Missouri, federal, or other state law).

headings.title: Penalties for commercial dealings in unlawfully obtained cultural items
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history note, and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Distinguished from subsection 2 by covering cultural items obtained in violation of sections 194.400 to 194.410 knowingly appropriated/used for profit, sold, purchased, or transported for sale or profit: class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for a second or subsequent violation (see section 194.400(5)).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history note (L. 1995 H.B. 160 § 578.157, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Elements of abandonment of a corpse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1995 H.B. 160 § 578.157, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Defines the offense as abandoning, disposing, deserting, or leaving a corpse without properly reporting the body's location to proper law enforcement officials in that county.

headings.title: Class E felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Classifies the offense of abandonment of a corpse as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Confirmed and explicitly retained the archived source discrepancy in sub 1 opening with 'Except as otherwise provided for in this subsection,' even though the emergency-vehicle (section 304.022) and law-enforcement-officer exceptions appear in sub 3 rather than within sub 1; checked lawful-lead-entry following and highest-degree-of-care duties in sub 2. All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Yielding right-of-way to organized funeral processions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270). Requires pedestrians and operators of all other vehicles to yield right-of-way to vehicles in an organized funeral procession; notes archived text opens with "Except as otherwise provided for in this subsection," though the exceptions appear in subsection 3 rather than inside subsection 1.

headings.title: Following lead vehicles and highest degree of care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs procession vehicles to follow a lawfully entering lead vehicle through an intersection notwithstanding state or local traffic control devices or right-of-way provisions, while exercising the highest degree of care toward other vehicles and pedestrians.

headings.title: Intersection right-of-way and emergency or officer exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants organized funeral processions right-of-way at all intersections regardless of traffic control devices, qualified by exceptions to yield to approaching emergency vehicles under section 304.022 or when directed by a law enforcement officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked practical-and-safe close following distance, mandatory flashing emergency lights for participating vehicles, and toll-free passage on toll bridges, tunnels, and highways. All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Safe close following distance in funeral processions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270). Directs vehicles in an organized funeral procession to follow the preceding vehicle as closely as is practical and safe under the conditions.

headings.title: Required flashing emergency lights during processions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits operating any vehicle as part of an organized funeral procession without its flashing emergency lights lighted.

headings.title: Toll-free passage on toll bridges, tunnels, and highways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides toll-free passage on all toll bridges, tunnels, and other toll highways to all vehicles in an organized funeral procession.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including sub 1(1)-(3)) and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Confirmed and explicitly retained the archived source cross-reference discrepancy in sub 1(2) citing 'the right-of-way granted in section 194.506' rather than section 194.503 (while sub 1(1) cites section 194.506(2) and sub 2 cites section 194.503), and verified infraction/$100 maximum fine in sub 3. Revised sub 1 to flag its law-enforcement, emergency-vehicle, and passing-lane exceptions, and revised sub 2 for concise neutral framing reflecting the non-crossing-path exception; retained sub 3.

headings.title: Prohibited maneuvers around funeral processions and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)-(3)) and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270). Bars nonparticipating vehicle operators from driving between moving procession vehicles with section 194.506(2) flashing lights (with law enforcement direction and emergency-vehicle signal exceptions), joining a procession to secure right-of-way (retaining archived source discrepancy citing "section 194.506" rather than section 194.503), or attempting to pass except where a passing lane is specifically provided.

headings.title: Entering intersections during red-signal procession passage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Bars nonparticipating vehicles from entering an intersection while an organized funeral procession proceeds through a red signal as permitted in section 194.503 unless doing so without crossing the procession's path.

headings.title: Infraction classification and maximum fine
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Classifies any violation of section 194.509 as an infraction punishable by a fine not exceeding one hundred dollars.

headings.title: Protection of amber-light motorcycle escorts from prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 270). Bars any ordinance, regulation, or other provision of law from prohibiting a motorcycle utilizing flashing amber lights to escort an organized funeral procession on the highway.

headings.title: Local authority to adopt substantially similar ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Uses permissive language ("may") allowing any city, town, village, or county to adopt an ordinance substantially similar to sections 194.500 to 194.512.
